# Judges Chapter 15 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), c. 1008 CE | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JDG_page_284.jpg, JDG_page_285.jpg

1. And it was after some days, in the days of the wheat harvest, Shimshon visited his wife with a kid of the goats. And he said, "Let me come in to my wife, to the chamber." But her father would not let him come in.

2. And her father said, "I surely said that you utterly hated her, and I gave her to your companion. Is not her younger sister more beautiful than she? Let her be yours instead."

3. And Shimshon said to them, "This time I am blameless before the P'lishtim when I do them harm."

4. And Shimshon went and caught three hundred foxes. And he took torches and turned tail to tail and put one torch between each pair of tails.

5. And he set fire to the torches and sent [them] into the standing grain of the P'lishtim. And he burned up both shocks and standing grain, and also the olive orchards.

6. And the P'lishtim said, "Who did this?" And they said, "Shimshon, the son-in-law of the Timnite, because he took his wife and gave her to his companion." And the P'lishtim went up and burned her and her father with fire.

7. And Shimshon said to them, "If you do like this, surely I will take vengeance on you, and after that I will cease."

8. And he struck them hip upon thigh, a great striking. And he went down and dwelt in the cleft of the rock of Etam.

9. And the P'lishtim went up and encamped in Y'hudah and spread out in Lechi.

10. And the men of Y'hudah said, "Why have you come up against us?" And they said, "To bind Shimshon we have come up, to do to him as he did to us."

11. And three thousand men of Y'hudah went down to the cleft of the rock of Etam and said to Shimshon, "Do you not know that the P'lishtim [are] rulers over us? And what [is] this you have done to us?" And he said to them, "As they did to me, so I did to them."

12. And they said to him, "To bind you we have come down, to give you into the hand of the P'lishtim." And Shimshon said to them, "Swear to me that you will not fall upon me yourselves."

13. And they said to him, saying, "No — we will only bind you and give you into their hand, but we will surely not kill you." And they bound him with two new ropes and brought him up from the rock.

14. He came to Lechi, and the P'lishtim shouted to meet him. And the Spirit of YHWH rushed upon him, and the ropes that [were] on his arms became like flax that has burned with fire, and his bonds melted from upon his hands.

15. And he found a fresh jawbone of a donkey, and he reached out his hand and took it, and he struck with it a thousand men.

16. And Shimshon said, "With the jawbone of a donkey — a heap, two heaps! With the jawbone of a donkey I struck a thousand men."

17. And it was, when he finished speaking, he threw the jawbone from his hand. And he called that place Ramat-Lechi.

18. And he was very thirsty, and he called to YHWH and said, "You have given this great salvation by the hand of your servant, and now shall I die of thirst and fall into the hand of the uncircumcised?"

19. And God split the hollow place that [is] in Lechi, and water came out from it. And he drank, and his spirit returned, and he revived. Therefore he called its name Ein-haq-Qore, which [is] in Lechi, to this day.

20. And he judged Yisrael in the days of the P'lishtim twenty years.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

1. **v.4 — "foxes":** shu'alim — can mean "foxes" or "jackals." Jackals are more likely as they travel in packs and are easier to catch.

2. **v.16 — "a heap, two heaps":** chamor chamoratayim — a pun. The word for "donkey" (chamor) sounds like "heap" (chomer). Samson plays with the double meaning: "With a donkey's jawbone — a donkey-heap, two donkey-heaps!" The wordplay is untranslatable.

3. **v.19 — "the hollow place that is in Lechi":** hammakhtesh asher-baLechi — the same place name Lechi means "jawbone." God splits a hollow in "Jawbone" to provide water — the geography itself becomes part of the wordplay.

— EMET, AI Translator
